_comment: Every entry needs a reason. Prefer naming specific functions over
excluding a whole file: most files that contain an untestable entrypoint
also contain testable helpers, and a file-wide exclusion hides those from
Exclusions are validated. An entry that matches no file, or names a
function that no longer exists, fails the run — so this list cannot rot

exclusions.reason: protoc-generated. Regenerated by `make proto-gen`; not hand-written and not ours to test. Also excluded from the LOC bar in scripts/loc-coverage-chart.py.
Multi-call binary entrypoint: dispatches os.Args to an applet's Main and exits. Nothing to assert that the applet tests do not already cover.
Developer tool whose whole body is func main(): flag parsing then a call into internal/lidar/l9endpoints/recorder, which is covered directly.
Developer tool whose whole body is func main(): reads a VRLOG via the recorder package and prints a summary. The replay logic it drives is covered in internal/lidar/l9endpoints/recorder.
func main() wrapper: opens the DB and calls into backfill.go, which is tested separately in the same package.
func main() wrapper. All the logic lives in run(), which takes its os.Stat, DB-open and backfill dependencies as parameters and is tested directly in the same package.
Test-only helper (NewTestDB) compiled into the package for other packages' tests. Exercised constantly, but by tests outside internal/db, so it never registers in this package's own profile.
Build-tag stub for builds without the pcap tag. The real implementation in the pcap-tagged file is what carries the logic.
Build-tag stub for builds without the pcap tag; selfCheckLibpcap is a no-op here. The failure path is covered by TestRunSelfCheckFailsWhenLiveCaptureRequestedWithoutPcap.

Process entrypoints: flag registration, server construction, signal handling and goroutine wiring, terminating in log.Fatalf/os.Exit and a blocking wg.Wait. Testing them means running the server. The rest of the file — the serial snapshot helpers, tailscaleServeTarget, and the visualiser/HINT adapters — stays in scope.
